reviews.decision_reason: The visible select_demand implementation selects every corpus row with demand_score >= 3, which includes all eight supplied records, but the assigned job output contains only the required top demand record n06-r01. This over-selection would pass generic keyword-like needs downstream instead of the deterministic recommendation input.

normalize preserves the over-selected eight-row input and only applies column normalization, allowed-id filtering, and an eight-row cap. The local transformation matches its declared role, but its output is contaminated by the upstream selection fault, so it is not independently reusable for reporting the final demand claim.

assemble_provenance deterministically ranks the normalized rows, but because the normalized input carries all eight selected records, its eight-row provenance table contradicts the one-row assigned job output. The ranking logic itself is not shown to introduce the first behavioral fault.
